clue.text: Feeling of dismay with smile after tea

indicators.note: after tells us the smile piece is placed behind the tea piece rather than in clue order

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
a broad smile

explanation.surface: Someone's dismay is softened by a smile over a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is annoyance or distress at having been humiliated or disappointed, a close synonym for dismay.

clue.text: Ability to engage with Northern church

parts.note: to engage (in a contest) is to compete
standard abbreviation for northern
Church of England, the usual crossword church

explanation.surface: A talent for getting involved with a church in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Competence is the capacity to do something well, a straightforward synonym for ability.

clue.text: Gas industry talk starting late

indicators.note: a word that starts late has lost its opening, so its first letter is missing

parts.note: specialist language of a trade or profession

explanation.surface: Shop talk in the gas industry only gets going late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the J from the front of the trade-talk word to leave the noble gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is an inert noble gas, element 18, so it is an example of a gas.

clue.text: Unusual recital is true to life

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters are put into an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An offbeat concert performance is praised for its lifelike quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Realistic describes a representation that is lifelike and accurate, matching the idiom true to life.

clue.text: In turning up one idiot, finding another

definitions.note: another idiot, picking up the idiot in the wordplay

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a twit is a silly person

explanation.surface: Turning up one fool only leads you to find another.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'another', meaning another idiot: the wordplay builds one idiot word inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a foolish or stupid person, so it is indeed another word for an idiot.

clue.text: Lentil dish picked up for children's author

indicators.note: something picked up is caught by the ear, so we want a word that sounds the same

parts.note: dal (dhal) is an Indian lentil dish

explanation.surface: A lentil curry is collected to feed a writer of children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl wrote Charlie and the Chocolate Factory and Matilda, so he is a famous children's author.

clue.text: Boy am I dumb turning over this builder's carrier

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a hod is the trough a builder uses to carry bricks

explanation.surface: A builder kicks himself for flipping over his brick carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points at the answer itself: reversing the answer gives the builder's carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: D'oh is Homer Simpson's exclamation on realising he has done something stupid, i.e. how dumb am I.

clue.text: Difficulty dropping duke's race horse equipment

indicators.note: dropping means letting something fall away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: hardness: the quality of being hard or difficult
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A troublesome duke drops out of the race, leaving his horse's tack behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the D from the difficulty word.
explanation.definitionFit: A harness is the set of straps attaching a horse to a cart or sulky, as used in harness racing.

clue.text: Hold up cup

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to rob someone in the street
second meaning: a large drinking cup

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests raising a trophy; in fact the first part is the robbery sense of hold up.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug someone is to rob them with threat of violence, and a mug is also a tall cup for hot drinks.

clue.text: Literary rascal perhaps cracked up on the air

indicators.note: something cracked up is broken into pieces, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A roguish character in a book has a breakdown during a live broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the rascal as only one kind of such a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a central character lacking heroic virtues, of whom a lovable literary rogue is one example.

clue.text: Beery in-law's drunk strong ale

indicators.note: a drunk person is all over the place, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A beer-loving relative by marriage is drunk on strong ale.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Barley wine is a very strong, rich English-style ale, despite its name not a wine at all.

clue.text: Running small broadcast leads to boredom

indicators.note: broadcast words are heard on air, so we go by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a machine that is running is on, and wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Turning a short run into a broadcast event ends up being tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, the two pieces sound like the French borrowing, pronounced on-WEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a listless weariness from lack of interest, a French loan word for boredom.

clue.text: Beer with strange name in area of Rio

parts.note: India pale ale, a type of beer

indicators.note: strange means odd or unfamiliar, so the letters take on an unfamiliar arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A beer with an odd name is served in a district of Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipanema is a beachside neighbourhood of Rio de Janeiro, famous from the song The Girl from Ipanema.

clue.text: Embitters one Republican motel owner Norman

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
R is the abbreviation for Republican
Norman Bates runs the Bates Motel in Hitchcock's Psycho

explanation.surface: A Republican and a sinister motel keeper together sour someone's mood.
explanation.definitionFit: To acerbate is to make bitter or exasperate, so acerbates is a synonym of embitters.

clue.text: Some threw a stereo, old printers, and computers, say

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words, so the answer sits inside them

parts.note: found across the three words

explanation.surface: Someone dumped a stereo along with old printers and computers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the printers and computers as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: E-waste is discarded electronic equipment, of which old printers and computers are typical examples.

clue.text: Clothing: dismay when note found inside

indicators.note: found inside says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to appal is to dismay or horrify
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: One's outfit causes dismay when a note is discovered inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for clothes or garments, making it a synonym for clothing.

clue.text: Ship five initial pieces of extra spicy salami: eat lots

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: initial pieces are the opening letters of each of the following words

parts.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Aboard a ship, someone tucks into extra-spicy salami.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is any ship or large boat, a standard synonym.

clue.text: Innocent U.S. lawyer gets overseas letter

parts.note: a lamb is a symbol of innocence
district attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A guileless American attorney receives a letter from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overseas' points to a foreign alphabet: here the Greek one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet, a letter used overseas.

clue.text: Computer test used in diagnostic: apt challenge

indicators.note: used in says the answer is contained within the following words

parts.note: spans the three words

explanation.surface: A computer check employed in a diagnostic routine is a fitting challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A CAPTCHA is an online test that tells humans from bots, typically distorted text or picture grids.

clue.text: Friend with lots of flowers about to bloom?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pal or mate

definitions.text: with lots of flowers about to bloom?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: full of buds

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second sense: a plant covered in unopened flowers could be called this.
explanation.definitionFit: A buddy is an informal word for a close friend, and adding -y to bud gives a jokey adjective for bud-covered.

clue.text: River feature's made-up detail I ignored

indicators.note: made-up means invented or fabricated, so the letters are rebuilt in a new arrangement
something ignored is left out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A description of a river is called fiction because one detail was ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A delta is the fan of land and channels formed where a river deposits silt at its mouth.

clue.text: Outlaw carved up hip to rib

indicators.note: carved up means cut into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A villain slashes someone from the hip to the rib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' looks like a noun for a bandit, but it is the verb meaning to ban.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlaw something is to make it illegal, which is to prohibit it.

clue.text: Garden tool cut off the top of footwear

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, and cutting it off removes it

parts.note: a shoe is an item of footwear

explanation.surface: A gardener uses a tool to slice the top off a boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoe is a long-handled gardening implement for weeding and breaking up soil.

clue.text: Ring of flowers put down we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so we go by sound

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down

explanation.surface: A garland of flowers is laid down, so we hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn round the neck, a ring of blooms.

clue.text: German water found in Amstel beer

indicators.note: found in says the answer lies inside the following words

parts.note: spans the two words

explanation.surface: German water is discovered in a Dutch lager.
explanation.walkthrough: Amstel is a Dutch beer brand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elbe is a major river flowing through Germany to the North Sea, so a body of German water.

clue.text: Exposed to risk alongside vampire killer

parts.note: at in the sense of by or next to, as in at the door
a wooden stake through the heart kills a vampire

explanation.surface: Someone standing beside a vampire slayer is in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at stake is in jeopardy, liable to be lost, which matches being exposed to risk.
